title: Erdős' Probabilistic Ramsey Lower Bound R(k,k) > n via the Property B Template
description: Answers open question oq-02 of property-b-first-moment: reuse the exact first-moment counting template of the Property B proof to formalize Erdős' classical 1947 diagonal Ramsey lower bound. If C(n,k)·2^(1-C(k,2)) < 1 — cleared of the fraction, C(n,k)·2 < 2^(C(k,2)) for k ≥ 2 — then there is a red/blue 2-coloring of the edges of the complete graph K_n with no monochromatic k-clique, hence R(k,k) > n. The key structural observation is that this is *literally* the Property B theorem applied to a derived hypergraph: the vertices being 2-colored are the EDGES of K_n (Edge P := {e : Finset P // e.card = 2}), and each k-subset S contributes one hyperedge — the bundle edgesWithin S of its C(k,2) internal edges. A coloring is monochromatic on the clique S exactly when it is `Mono` on that bundle, the parent file's notion verbatim, so the parent's exact count `card_mono` (2·2^(N-t) colorings are monochromatic on a t-edge bundle) and its first moment principle `exists_zero_of_sum_lt_card` carry the whole argument. The only genuinely new content is the combinatorial identity |edgesWithin S| = C(|S|,2). Verified, 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide.

meta.author: Paul Erdős (1947), formalized in Lean 4

mathlibDependencies.description: #(powersetCard n s) = C(#s, n). Supplies both halves of the count: the number of k-cliques is #(powersetCard k univ) = C(n,k), and (via the image bijection) the number of edges inside a clique S is #(powersetCard 2 S) = C(|S|,2).

#(s.image f) = #s for injective f. With f = Subtype.val on Edge P, it transfers the count of edgesWithin S to the count of its image, the set of 2-subsets of S, identifying |edgesWithin S| with #(powersetCard 2 S).

The parent file's exact count: exactly 2·2^(N - |bundle|) colorings are monochromatic on a nonempty edge bundle. Reused verbatim with the 'vertex' type instantiated to Edge P — this is the 'same counting template' the open question asks for.

The parent's first moment principle: a nonnegative integer statistic summing to less than the number of outcomes vanishes somewhere. Applied to the statistic 'number of monochromatic k-cliques' over the 2^(C(n,2)) edge-colorings.
Swaps the sum over colorings with the sum over k-cliques — the linearity-of-expectation step that turns ∑_colorings #(mono cliques) into ∑_cliques #(mono colorings).

originalContributions: ramsey_lower_bound: a self-contained, 0-axiom Lean proof of Erdős' 1947 probabilistic diagonal Ramsey lower bound — if C(n,k)·2 < 2^(C(k,2)) then there is an edge 2-coloring c : Edge P → Bool of K_n under which no k-subset of the vertices is monochromatic, hence R(k,k) > n. The proof is obtained by re-running the Property B first-moment template with the 'vertices' being the edges of K_n and the 'hyperedges' being the C(k,2)-edge bundles of the k-cliques.

card_edgesWithin: the combinatorial identity |edgesWithin S| = C(|S|,2), the one genuinely new ingredient. Proved by carrying edgesWithin S bijectively (via Subtype.val, injective) onto powersetCard 2 S — the 2-subsets of S — and applying card_powersetCard. No explicit pairing of vertices is constructed.

Edge P := {e : Finset P // e.card = 2}: modeling the edges of the complete graph K_n as a Fintype, so that an edge 2-coloring is simply a function Edge P → Bool and the parent's vertex-coloring template applies unchanged with V := Edge P.

MonoClique S c := Mono (edgesWithin S) c: recognizing 'the clique on S is monochromatic' as the parent file's `Mono` predicate on the derived vertex set, which is exactly what lets card_mono be reused verbatim.

A clean reduction of the threshold C(n,k)·2·2^(N-C(k,2)) < 2^N to the dimensionless C(n,k)·2 < 2^(C(k,2)) (equivalently C(n,k)·2^(1-C(k,2)) < 1) using only 2^N = 2^(C(k,2))·2^(N-C(k,2)) with C(k,2) ≤ N established by edgesWithin S ⊆ univ — the ambient edge count N = C(n,2) is never computed.

The point type P is an arbitrary Fintype with DecidableEq, n = Fintype.card P; the sample space is the full edge-coloring space Edge P → Bool. #print axioms reports only the foundational propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound for ramsey_lower_bound, exists_ramsey_coloring, and card_edgesWithin — no sorryAx, no Lean.ofReduceBool.

overview.historicalContext: In 1947 Erdős gave a one-paragraph probabilistic proof that the diagonal Ramsey number grows at least exponentially: R(k,k) > n whenever C(n,k)·2^(1-C(k,2)) < 1, which yields R(k,k) > 2^(k/2) (up to lower-order factors). The argument is the founding example of the probabilistic method in combinatorics — color the C(n,2) edges of the complete graph K_n red/blue independently at random; a fixed k-subset is monochromatic with probability 2·2^(-C(k,2)); so the expected number of monochromatic k-cliques is C(n,k)·2^(1-C(k,2)); when this is below 1 some coloring has none. The lower bound R(k,k) ≥ (1+o(1))·(k/(e√2))·2^(k/2) (Spencer's Lovász-Local-Lemma refinement) and the recent breakthrough upper bound R(k,k) ≤ (4-ε)^k (Campos–Griffiths–Morris–Sahasrabudhe, 2023) bracket the truth, but Erdős' 1947 exponential lower bound remains the prototype. This entry formalizes it as a direct instance of the Property B first-moment template.
overview.problemStatement: Let P be a finite vertex set with n = |P| points, and let k ≥ 2. If $\binom{n}{k}\,2^{\,1-\binom{k}{2}} < 1$ — equivalently $\binom{n}{k}\cdot 2 < 2^{\binom{k}{2}}$ — then there is a 2-coloring $c$ of the edges of the complete graph $K_n$ such that no $k$-element subset $S$ of $P$ is monochromatic (the clique on $S$ contains both an edge of each color). Consequently the diagonal Ramsey number satisfies $R(k,k) > n$.
overview.text: Color the C(n,2) edges of K_n red/blue at random. A fixed k-subset S spans C(k,2) edges and is monochromatic with probability 2·2^(-C(k,2)). The expected number of monochromatic k-subsets is therefore C(n,k)·2·2^(-C(k,2)) = C(n,k)·2^(1-C(k,2)). When this is below 1 the integer count of monochromatic cliques must be zero for some coloring — a Ramsey witness. The work is the exact count of how many edge-colorings are monochromatic on a fixed clique, which the Property B file already supplies once one realizes the edges of K_n play the role of its 'vertices'.
overview.proofStrategy:
Model the edges of K_n as Edge P := {e : Finset P // e.card = 2}, a Fintype; an edge 2-coloring is a function c : Edge P → Bool. For a vertex set S, the bundle of internal edges is edgesWithin S = {e : Edge P | (e : Finset P) ⊆ S}.

1. **Edge count of a clique (card_edgesWithin).** |edgesWithin S| = C(|S|,2). Subtype.val carries edgesWithin S injectively onto powersetCard 2 S (the 2-subsets of S), so the count follows from card_image_of_injective and card_powersetCard. This is the only new ingredient.

2. **Per-clique color count (reuse card_mono).** Define MonoClique S c := Mono (edgesWithin S) c, the parent file's monochromaticity predicate on the derived 'vertex' set Edge P. The parent's card_mono gives, for |S| = k (so the bundle is nonempty since C(k,2) ≥ 1 when k ≥ 2), exactly 2·2^(N − C(k,2)) colorings monochromatic on S, where N = |Edge P| = C(n,2).

3. **Linearity / Fubini.** ∑_c #(monochromatic k-cliques) = ∑_{S ∈ powersetCard k univ} #{c : MonoClique S c} = C(n,k)·2·2^(N−C(k,2)), via card_filter + sum_comm (the parent's exact pattern) and #(powersetCard k univ) = C(n,k).

4. **Threshold.** The sample space has 2^N colorings. With C(k,2) ≤ N (because edgesWithin S ⊆ univ), 2^N = 2^(C(k,2))·2^(N−C(k,2)), so the incidence total C(n,k)·2·2^(N−C(k,2)) is < 2^N exactly when C(n,k)·2 < 2^(C(k,2)) — the hypothesis. The ambient count N = C(n,2) is never evaluated.

5. **First moment (reuse exists_zero_of_sum_lt_card).** Since the incidence total is below the number of colorings, some coloring c has zero monochromatic k-cliques; its monochromatic-clique filter is empty, so no k-subset is monochromatic under c. The case of no k-cliques at all (k > n) is handled vacuously.
keyInsights: **Ramsey's lower bound is Property B in disguise.** Coloring the edges of K_n and forbidding a monochromatic k-clique is exactly 2-coloring a hypergraph whose vertices are the edges of K_n and whose hyperedges are the C(k,2)-edge bundles of the k-cliques. The Property B theorem applies with V := Edge P unchanged.

**The only new lemma is |edgesWithin S| = C(|S|,2).** Once the edges-as-vertices reinterpretation is made, the entire probabilistic content — the per-clique count and the first moment step — is imported verbatim from the parent file; the clique edge-count is the single genuinely new computation.

**The ambient edge count C(n,2) never appears.** Keeping N = |Edge P| abstract and using only C(k,2) ≤ N (from edgesWithin S ⊆ univ) avoids ever computing |Edge P| = C(n,2), so the threshold reduces cleanly to the dimensionless C(n,k)·2 < 2^(C(k,2)).

**The fraction clears to an integer inequality.** C(n,k)·2^(1-C(k,2)) < 1 is exactly C(n,k)·2 < 2^(C(k,2)) for k ≥ 2 (where C(k,2) ≥ 1), so the whole proof stays in ℕ with no real-valued probability — first moment is again integer pigeonhole.

**Reuse, not re-derivation, is the point.** The open question asked for 'the same counting template'; importing card_mono and exists_zero_of_sum_lt_card and reinstantiating the vertex type demonstrates the template's reach across two of the probabilistic method's founding theorems.

sections.title: The Ramsey Lower Bound (Same Template as Property B)
sections.summary: ramsey_lower_bound: after dispatching the no-clique case vacuously, the per-clique count is the parent's card_mono on the C(k,2)-edge bundle (nonempty since k ≥ 2). The incidence total ∑_c #(mono cliques) = C(n,k)·2·2^(N−C(k,2)) by card_filter + sum_comm; the threshold reduces to C(n,k)·2 < 2^(C(k,2)) using 2^N = 2^(C(k,2))·2^(N−C(k,2)) with C(k,2) ≤ N from edgesWithin S ⊆ univ; exists_zero_of_sum_lt_card then yields a coloring with no monochromatic clique.

sections.title: Corollary: R(k,k) > n as a Ramsey Witness
sections.summary: exists_ramsey_coloring restates ramsey_lower_bound as a Ramsey witness quantified over all k-element subsets of P directly, rather than over the powersetCard k univ Finset, giving the R(k,k) > n reading.

conclusion.summary: Erdős' 1947 probabilistic diagonal Ramsey lower bound — R(k,k) > n whenever C(n,k)·2^(1-C(k,2)) < 1 — formalized with zero sorries and zero axioms as a direct instance of the Property B first-moment template. The edges of K_n play the role of the 'vertices' being 2-colored and the k-cliques play the role of the hyperedges; the parent file's exact monochromatic count card_mono and first moment principle exists_zero_of_sum_lt_card are reused verbatim, and the single new lemma |edgesWithin S| = C(|S|,2) supplies the clique edge-count.
conclusion.implications: This entry answers open question oq-02 of property-b-first-moment and supplies the genuine erdos_ramsey_lower_bound that prob-method-expectation advertises but leaves trivial. More broadly it demonstrates that the Property B counting template is not special to hypergraph 2-colorability: re-instantiating the 'vertex' type with the edges of K_n recovers the founding theorem of the probabilistic method, Erdős' exponential Ramsey lower bound, with the only new work being an elementary clique edge-count.
openQuestions: Derive an explicit numerical consequence such as R(k,k) > 2^(k/2) by exhibiting an n with C(n,k)·2 < 2^(C(k,2)), e.g. via the standard estimate C(n,k) ≤ n^k/k! and n = ⌊2^(k/2)⌋.
Prove the asymmetric off-diagonal lower bound for R(s,t) > n via the same template with two different monochromatic-clique sizes, weighting the red and blue events separately.
